title: Volta's own question (inspired by: Arbitrage-Free Implied Volatility Surface Reconstruction via; Arithmetic Models for Commodity Futures, Vanilla, and Calend)
idea: On days when the short‑term IV term structure is steep (term > 1.1) but the implied event move is modest (event_prem ≤ 1), does the Nasdaq‑100 session range tend to be larger relative to its 20‑day average range?

spec.question: On days when the short‑term IV term structure is steep (term > 1.1) but the implied event move is modest (event_prem ≤ 1), does the Nasdaq‑100 session range tend to be larger relative to its 20‑day average range?
spec.explain: The term column captures the steepness of the IV curve (7d IV / 30d IV). Prior research asked about steep term together with large event‑premiums. I want to see the opposite situation: a steep term but no big event, and whether that combination still leads to an amplified intraday range.

verdict: PROMISING (stress test: survived) : FACT: average 1.03, median 0.907 over 2906 sessions (2014-19: 1.03, 2020-25: 1.03). Predictor: lowest-fifth days 0.916 vs highest-fifth 1.29, skill +7.3% vs the base rate, better in 9/9 unseen years
how: Q: On days when the short‑term IV term structure is steep (term > 1.1) but the implied event move is modest (event_prem ≤ 1), does the Nasdaq‑100 session range tend to be larger relative to its 20‑day average range? | answer = `y_range / k_range20` | predicted by `term * (1 - clip(event_prem, 0, 1))` | stress: skill +7.30; nudged formulas kept >= half the skill in 5/6; stale copies (lag 1-12 months) clearly worse in 4/4
